technical_hypothesis.primary_training_data_risk: student speech, handwriting and practical demonstrations vary by age, region, disability, device, noise, task and teaching context; expert labels and consented representative samples are not established

training_data.observation_unit: one consented student assessment artifact captured for a defined task and rubric
training_data.input_data: audio waveform or image/video capture, task prompt, grade or course context, capture-quality metadata, rubric and only the context available at assessment time
training_data.target_or_reward: expert-annotated reading events, legibility and response structure, or observed practical steps; final pedagogical judgment remains human
training_data.label_source: double-reviewed teacher, literacy-specialist or instructor annotations; availability and inter-rater agreement are unknown
training_data.prediction_time: after guided capture and before specialist correction or pedagogical decision
training_data.expected_volume: unknown and network-specific; sufficient coverage across grades, regions, devices and learner profiles must be measured before training
training_data.class_balance: unknown; uncommon speech patterns, disabilities, rare handwriting forms and unsafe or omitted practical steps may be underrepresented
training_data.historical_coverage: unknown; current assessment data may contain scores without reusable raw audio, images, video, consent or aligned annotations
training_data.train_validation_split: student-disjoint and school-disjoint holdouts, plus region, device, grade, task and time-based holdouts
training_data.leakage_risks: final score, teacher correction, remediation assignment, answer key markup or post-assessment transcript included in model inputs
training_data.representativeness_risks: regional accents, bilingual students, disabilities, age, literacy stage, camera and microphone quality, handwriting tools, classroom noise and vocational equipment
training_data.feedback_loop: automated flags can influence teacher attention and annotation density, changing future labels and apparent error rates
training_data.privacy_and_usage_constraints: student voice, image, video and educational records require minimization, purpose limitation, access control, retention rules, consent or other valid legal basis, and prohibition of autonomous high-stakes grading
training_data.fallback_if_data_is_insufficient: guided capture, deterministic audio and image quality checks, structured rubrics, sampling, double correction, teacher review and adoption of validated existing assessment platforms

portfolio_comparison.reason: Reading-fluency automation is already commercially available in Brazil; handwriting correction remains a rubric and teacher-review extension; practical video assessment repeats multimodal recognition and evidence-review patterns already represented. None exposes a distinct actor-process-capability-outcome combination sufficient for publication.

existing_landscape.summary: Adopt validated reading-fluency platforms where appropriate and preserve guided capture, deterministic quality controls, structured rubrics and specialist review. Treat handwriting or practical-action recognition only as bounded experiments inside existing assessment workflows, not separate opportunities.

research.findings: Brazilian 2025 reading-fluency microdata and current commercial platforms confirm a real assessment workflow and existing AI-assisted offerings. Recent Brazilian research shows technical feasibility for automated fluency measures but explicitly requires further empirical validation across real educational contexts. The remaining handwriting and practical-video candidates are optional recognition layers with strong representativeness, privacy and pedagogical-validity constraints rather than materially differentiated repository opportunities.

where_ai_enters.primary_mechanism: specialized speech, handwriting or video recognition to generate bounded assessment evidence for specialist review
where_ai_enters.human_control: teachers and specialists retain scoring, diagnosis, intervention, accommodation and any consequential educational decision
